investigations.question: When a node restarts with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled over a commit-tracking log store, is the configuration it afterwards uses for elections and for counting committed support the committed configuration recorded in its own log, and what do a divergent reconstruction and the resulting support context do to decisions and progress?
investigations.hypothesis: NewRaft re-derives Raft's own configuration only from configuration-carrying log entries above max(lastSnapshotIndex, lastApplied); because restoreFromCommittedLogs advances lastApplied to the store's tracked commit index before that scan, a committed configuration entry at or below that index is never re-derived, so the restarted node keeps the configuration installed from snapshot metadata (or none at all when no snapshot exists) and then judges its own eligibility and support against that stale context.
investigations.discriminator: Every consequence in this account is exercised, including what a healed partition leaves behind, and the strongest one has been reproduced. What remains outside is the surrounding fault and storage model: a disk-backed commit-tracking store, crash and restart timing, and further repetitions or longer runs. Those are recorded as limitations rather than as open questions.

knowledge.statement: A restart with Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled over a commit-tracking log store reconstructs a configuration that is not the one recorded in the node's own log whenever the tracked commit index covers that node's last configuration entry, in both directions and across five exercised shapes: the no-snapshot case reported latest_config_index 0 with no servers against a single-voter entry at log index 1; the snapshot-then-remove case reported the snapshot's two voters, one of them the peer removed at log index 103, against the single-voter entry there; the snapshot-then-promote case reported one voter, the promoted peer still carried as a nonvoter, against the two-voter entry at log index 104; the demote/promote ladder reported one voter against committed entries of three voters and of five voters; and a peer that had snapshotted itself while still a voter reported three voters after its vote had been removed in the committed configuration, where it holds none. knowledge.conditions: NewRaft restart over the same log, stable and snapshot stores; RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and the log store implements CommitTrackingLogStore; the node's last configuration entry is either inside the applied prefix replayed from the tracked commit index (divergence, in either direction) or above it (correct reconstruction); the snapshot that supplies the wrong configuration may have been taken by the leader or by the restarting peer itself; no membership change is issued after the restart.

scope.description: Restart reconstruction of a Raft node's own configuration: four in-process cases over the captured package's own test facilities, pairing RestoreCommittedLogs enabled and disabled within two single-voter committed shapes. Each case applies 100 commands through the leader, optionally snapshots and then commits RemoveServer for the non-leader peer, reads the configuration entry and tracked commit index from the surviving instance's own log store, stops every instance, and restarts the surviving voter with NewRaft over the same log, stable and snapshot stores plus a fresh in-memory transport.
assumptions: Real raft instances in one process over the in-memory transport and the in-memory commit-tracking log store from the captured package; the same durable stores are reused across the restart and no other instance is left running to send entries.

In both shapes the committed configuration after the setup is a single-voter configuration: the bootstrap configuration (1 voter) with no snapshot, or a snapshot taken before a committed RemoveServer that leaves 1 voter while the snapshot metadata still holds 2.
The bounded progress window is 3000 ms (60 x ElectionTimeout = 50 ms, HeartbeatTimeout = 50 ms) and the flag-disabled control runs the identical setup for each shape.
excluded: Disk-backed stores, real networks, process crashes during the restart, and post-restart client membership changes or snapshot installs that could rewrite the configuration.

basis.prefix: The single generated test builds each case with MakeClusterCustom(MakeClusterOpts{Peers: 1 or 2, Bootstrap: true, CommitTrackingLogs: true, Conf: inmemConfig with TrailingLogs 10 and RestoreCommittedLogs set per case}), applies 100 commands through the elected leader, and for the second shape calls leader.Snapshot() followed by leader.RemoveServer(non-leader ID) plus 10 more applies. Before the restart it reads, from the surviving instance's own stores, the last configuration-carrying log entry (index, decoded server list) together with the snapshot metadata's ConfigurationIndex and server list and the commit-tracking store's staged commit index; it then shuts down every instance and restarts the survivor with NewRaft over the same stores and a fresh in-memory transport wrapped in a counter for RequestPreVote/RequestVote. basis.responsibility: NewRaft owns the reconstruction of a node's own configuration from its durable stores, and the reconstructed configurations.latest is the only input to the node's own election gating, quorumSize and leader commitment; no component outside Raft is required to repair it.
